records.title: Fordham Theatre Mainstage: "Measure for Measure"
records.venue_name: Pope Auditorium
records.description:
Join us for our Second Mainstage Production of the Year!
Directed by Bobbin Ramsey and written by William Shakespeare,
Measure for Measure
is an intellectual and political thriller that grapples with moral hypocrisy and abuse of power. When her brother Claudio is sentenced to death under a long-forgotten law, a young novitiate, Isabella, pleads for mercy from the unyielding authoritarian, Angelo. What follows is a dangerous battle between morality and desire, as Shakespeare exposes the hypocrisy lurking beneath the surface of power.
See
here
for tickets!

records.title: Lecture: “No Logos: Exilic Theory of Talmud” by Elad Lapidot
records.venue_name: McMahon Hall, 109
records.description: A talk by Elad Lapidot, Professor for Hebraic Studies at the University of Lille, considering Jewishness as a tradition of thought rather than endangered life, focused on talmudic literature as a distinct method of thinking that diverges from the philosophical logos of the polis.

records.title: Lecture: "Spectral and Timing Signatures of Black Hole and Neutron Star Sources Observations and Theory
records.venue_name: Freeman Hall, 103 (approximate meeting point)
records.description:
Abstract
To demonstrate that in x-ray observations there is objective and model independent information regarding the nature of the compact objects (Black Hole and Neutron Sources).  To illuminate the status of our results with respect to the recent observations of these sources.
Guest Speaker:
Lev Titarchuk, PhD
Lev Titarchuk worked in the Space Research Institute in Moscow, Russia, in the Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, in Naval Research Laboratory, Washington DC and University of Ferrara, in Italy.  He is now affiliated with INFN, in Rome, Italy.

records.title: Becoming in the African Megacity: Housing, Mobility, and the Unmaking of the Apartheid City
records.venue_name: Lowenstein Center, LL 914
records.description:
The Graduate Program in Urban Studies invites you to a special lecture by Stephan de Beer, director of the Centre for Faith and Community and professor of practical and urban theology at the University of Pretoria, South Africa.
This lecture will explore questions of housing, mobility, and urban transformation in the African megacity, with particular attention to migration and the ongoing reshaping of cities shaped by apartheid.
There will be a reception following the lecture. RSVP's are not required for this event.

records.title: Praying for a Non-Nuclear World
records.venue_name: University Church (approximate meeting point)
records.description:
​Join American and Japanese Catholic leaders as they celebrate Mass on the occasion of the U.N review of the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW).
​The liturgy will be followed by a discussion with the audience about critical efforts by Pope Leo XIV and the Catholic Church around the world to push for nuclear disarmament amid rising global tensions.
​A relic from the atomic bombing of Nagasaki, the head of the virgin known as Our Lady of Nagasaki, or
Hibaku no Maria
, will also be on display in Fordham’s University Church. This will be one of the rare occasions the cherished fragment has been out of Japan since the atomic bombing of Japan by the U.S. in 1945.
​Celebrants will include:
​
Archbishop Peter Michiaki Nakamura of Nagasaki
, where the second American atomic bomb was detonated on August 9, 1945.
​
Archbishop John Wester of Santa Fe
, a leading voice for nuclear disarmament in the U.S. hierarchy
​
Archbishop Paul Etienne of Seattle,
also a leading episcopal advocate for a nuclear-free world
​
Catholics and non-Catholics, believers and nonbelievers, all are welcome to this service and opportunity to advocate for a nuclear-free world.

records.title: Christmas Movie Screening: "Merchants of Joy"
records.venue_name: McNally Amphitheatre
records.description:
​
Join Academy Award-winning filmmaker and Fordham grad Celia Aniskovich for a screening and discussion of her acclaimed documentary,
Merchants of Joy
, about the high-stakes New York sidewalk Christmas tree trade.
​
Celia Aniskovich’s film,
Merchants of Joy
,
premiered last Christmas on Amazon and follows the “five families” of New York City tree sales as they source, bargain and hustle, blending street smarts and holiday spirit.
Watch the trailer
here
.
​Celia graduated from Fordham Rose Hill in 2014 — you can read an interview with her senior self
here
— and has leveraged her degree in communications (and theology and philosophy) into
a remarkable career
as a
storyteller and filmmaker
.
​She will join in a discussion with the audience after the screening. Celia is also a lifelong Mets fan and is currently working on a film about the Amazins’ recent season. So she needs some Christmas joy — sign up!
​
Free hot chocolate and cookies — first come, first served!

records.title: RESCHEDULED: November Project WASTE
records.venue_name: Muskrat Cove Park — Woodlawn station entrance (approximate meeting point)
records.venue_address: Webster Avenue & East 233rd Street, Bronx, NY 10470
records.description:
This event was initially scheduled for November 13th.
Join us for our last Project WASTE event for 2026! This event is part of our hands-on outreach strategy which includes trash collection and assessment. As a volunteer, you will help our Ecology staff count, assess and remove trash from the Muskrat Cove trash boom so that we can categorize floatable trash into distinct categories while keeping the river clean. Information on the quantity, toxicity, material, and brands of trash will help to identify sources of pollution and to inform communities, businesses and municipal officials of this Bronx River problem.
The event will take place in-water at the Muskrat Cove trash boom. The activity will start around 10:00AM and last until 12:00PM. All materials will be provided. Nearby transportation includes the 2 train at 233rd Street and the Metro-North at Woodlawn.
The meeting location will be the entrance to the jogging path just to the left of the station parking lot.
Event Contact Info: Christian Murphy (917) 361-8922

records.title: Family Art Project: Tiny Terrariums
records.venue_name: Wave Hill — Meet at Wave Hill House (approximate meeting point)
records.description:
Explore the bustling world of tiny creatures in the dirt right beneath your feet. We'll learn about soil and decomposers as we craft mini jar habitats. While jars are provided, we encourage families to go green and bring their own glass or plastic containers from home.
Registration not required.
At 11:30am families can enjoy a storytime program in the Gund Theater, all ages welcome.
Wave Hill House is wheelchair-accessible. There is an accessible, ground-level entrance at the front of the building with a power-assist door. The restroom on the ground level is all-gender and ADA-compliant. Additional ADA-compliant restrooms are available on the lower level, which can be accessed by elevator.
Price
Free
with admission to the grounds

records.title: Garden Highlights Walk
records.venue_name: Wave Hill — Meet at Perkins Visitor Center (approximate meeting point)
records.description:
Join a knowledgeable Wave Hill Garden Guide for a leisurely stroll in the gardens. Topics vary by season and the expertise of the Guide--come back for an encore; each walk varies with the Guide leading it.
This walk lasts a half-hour to 45 minutes. Public Garden Walks are most appropriate for adults or young adults. Not intended for groups; groups should sign-up for
Private Garden Tours
.
Severe weather cancels. Registration not required for this drop-in event.
Questions? Please email us at
information@wavehill.org
or call 718.549.3200 x251.
Garden Highlights Walks follow a variety of routes along mixed-material pathways and varying elevations. Accessible routes are available as requested; please indicate your need to the Garden Guide.
Price
Free
with admission to the grounds

Free
with admission to the grounds

records.title: Mind-Builders Creative Arts Center Stage Band
records.venue_name: Wave Hill — Wave Hill House, Armor Hall (approximate meeting point)
records.description:
Join us for a performance by Mind-Builders Creative Arts Center Stage Band in collaboration with exhibiting artists Angel Nevarez and Valerie Tevere that reimagines music through experimentation, improvisation, and collective listening. Organized as part of the exhibition
As far as the ear can hear
and shaped by the artists' practice of reinterpreting musical traditions across genres and histories, the Stage Band will collaborate with Nevarez and Tevere to create a new composition that blends and reinterprets musical genres through collective experimentation and performance.
Founded in 2012,
Mind-Builders Creative Arts Center
Stage Band is comprised of a diverse group of students, ranging from ages 11 to over 70. Under the directorship of Christopher Palmer, these dedicated musicians have developed an extensive repertoire of featuring original arrangements and compositions that showcase a blending in different styles including jazz, RnB, Latin, rock, pop, and more. Their repertoire highlights such composers as Dizzy Gillespie, Duke Ellington, Charles Mingus, Stevie Wonder, amongst others. As an incubator for a next generation of Bronx music, musicians and creatives, the Stage Band has proudly been presented in several venues throughout New York City and the Bronx. Several members have blossomed into budding composers, with original songs integrated into the Band’s repertoire, and alum have gone on to pursue continued education in music in schools such as Purchase College. The Mind-Builders Stage Band is proudly known as the reigning champions of the High Note Festival and the Music in the Parks competitions, bringing home the gold trophies for four consecutive years.

Awaken your mind and body on a forest bathing walk through the winter gardens with certified nature therapy guide Cindy Olsen. Benefits include boosts to the immune system, cardiovascular strength-building, stress reduction, improvement to cognitive functioning, and deepening connections to nature and the self.
Space is limited; adults only, please. Severe weather cancels.
Registration required; online or by calling 718.549.3200 x251.
Questions? Please email us at
information@wavehill.org
or call the telephone number and extension above.
Walks follow a route along mixed-material pathways with varying elevations. Participants will be outdoors and moving around the gardens for most of the time. The event will conclude in an indoor space that is very large and open on the first floor of the building, with seating on the floor, or on chairs provided.
Price
Free
with admission to the grounds
Register

records.title: Sweater Mending with Needle Felting
records.venue_name: Wave Hill — Wave Hill House, Mark Twain Room (approximate meeting point)
records.description:
Have a woolen sweater in need of some TLC? Patch it up with your own applique in this cozy visible mending workshop with fiber artist J Hann. Mending is a simple and creative way to reduce waste and extend the life of the clothes you love. Using needle felting techniques, J Hann will guide participants in this workshop to bring a beloved sweater back to life or simply add color and texture to a garment in any shape.
Please bring a woolen or knitted sweater for mending. Synthetic fibers are trickier to mend but can be used.
Wave Hill House and Mark Twain are wheelchair-accessible. There is an accessible, ground-level entrance at the front of the building with a power-assist door. The restroom on the ground level is all-gender and ADA-compliant. Additional ADA-compliant restrooms are available on the lower level, which can be accessed by elevator.
Price
$40, including admission to the grounds. Wave Hill Members save 10%
Register

records.title: Winter Birding and Nature Journaling
records.venue_name: Wave Hill — Across the Grounds (approximate meeting point)
records.description:
The Hudson River Valley is home to an impressive diversity of bird species, even in the heart of winter. Join naturalist Gabriel Willow for a guided walk through Wave Hill’s garden to observe resident and migratory birds in their winter habitat. Birders of all experience levels are welcome.
Following the walk, take your observations to paper with guided nature journaling. Whether you choose to sketch or write, nature journaling offers a mindful way to reflect on your observations from the winter landscape. All materials provided, just bring your curiosity and willingness to slow down, observe, and capture the moment on paper.
Advance registration is encouraged. Day-of registration is based on availability and not guaranteed.
Questions? Please email
information@wavehill.org
or call 718.549.3200 x 251.
Walks follow a route along mixed-material pathways with varying elevations. A limited amount of walking sticks are available to borrow. Pace varies from a slow walk to moderate walk throughout.
Price
$25, Wave Hill Members save 10%
Register

records.title: Family Art Project: Maira's Marvelous Mural
records.venue_name: Wave Hill — Meet at Wave Hill House (approximate meeting point)
records.description:
What fascinating places can we map and explore? Let's draw inspiration from the renowned artist Maira Kalman’s mural of Wave Hill and transform our own neighborhoods into colorful and whimsical paintings.
Registration not required.
Wave Hill House is wheelchair-accessible. There is an accessible, ground-level entrance at the front of the building with a power-assist door. The restroom on the ground level is all-gender and ADA-compliant. Additional ADA-compliant restrooms are available on the lower level, which can be accessed by elevator.

Free
with admission to the grounds

records.title: Community Winter Yoga
records.venue_name: Wave Hill — Armor Hall (approximate meeting point)
records.description:
Kick off the new year with this free introductory class in Wave Hill’s grand Armor Hall. Certified yoga instructor Susie Caramanica guides participants through gentle movements to feel more connected and rejuvenated. All levels are welcome. While sheltered and warm, we'll be surrounded by a panoramic view of our Conifer Slope and majestic trees, offering an inspiring winter backdrop. This is a beginner-level class that can be modified.
Registration is not required.
Questions? Please contact us at
information@wavehill.org
or by calling the number and extension provided above.

Free

records.title: Open Hours at the Environmental Education Center (Weekends) – November 15
records.venue_name: Environmental Education Center
records.description:
Explore Brooklyn Bridge Park like never before during open hours at the Environmental Education Center.
The Environmental Education Center is open for free, drop-in hours at 99 Plymouth Street in Dumbo, Brooklyn! Get to know Brooklyn Bridge Park with monthly educational themes, a 250 gallon aquarium filled with critters from the East River, a 10’ scale model of Brooklyn Bridge Park, crafts, a reading corner, and much more.
Open Hours offer the opportunity for self-led investigation with guidance by expert educators to reveal the hidden stories found within and around Brooklyn Bridge Park.
Don’t miss our special program
Feed the Fauna
at
3:00 PM every Saturday.
Get up close with the Ed Center animals as they’re fed lunch! What do turtles eat? What about mud snails? And fish? Learn about our amazing animals’ habitats, characteristics, and diets.
Weekly on Thurs/Fri 3-5 PM, Sat/Sun 1-5 PM

records.title: Bargemusic Concerts – November 15
records.venue_name: Visitor Center at the Boathouse (approximate meeting point)
records.description:
For nearly 50 years, Bargemusic has been committed to attracting local audiences and enhancing the cultural life of New York by offering performances of chamber music in an intimate setting – the type of setting in which chamber music is meant to be heard.
To make this experience available to as many people as possible, all Bargemusic Concerts are Admission Free.
Check the
Bargemusic website
for details on the performance scheduled for each day.
Bargemusic concerts are 1 to 1.5 hours, with no intermission. Doors open 20 minutes before the concert (no tickets, no reservations). No food or drink is permitted inside the Boathouse, and no photo, video, or audio recording is allowed without permission. The Brooklyn Bridge Park Boathouse is wheelchair accessible, and restrooms are located adjacent to the performance room.
All concerts are Free Admission

records.title: Nature Journaling: Nests and Dreys
records.venue_name: Environmental Education Center
records.description:
Do you feel like you need a moment of pause and a deeper connection with nature? Join us on the first Saturday of each month for a free nature journaling workshop, as part of our
Peace In Nature
series. The 90-minute workshop helps you start or expand your nature journaling practice, providing you with ecological context, thematic prompts and time to journal.
As we head into the winter, December’s theme “Nests & Dreys” invites you to observe and reflect on the many shapes a home can take.
This series is intended for adults, but all are welcome. Materials are provided on a first-come, first-served basis, but we encourage you to bring your own materials and journals if you have them. This event is first come, first serve, with 20 total spots available. Advance registration encouraged but not required.
Register Now!
Accessibility Note: Please reach out to education@bbp.nyc for any accessibility needs or questions. The workshop will start indoors at the Environmental Education Center. The classroom has a low-pile carpet. Available seating options include stools and cushions on the rug. Bathrooms, with accessible stalls, are available in the building. In the education center, there is regular muted noise from trains above. Weather permitting, we will travel around 600 ft on asphalt paths to journaling locations nearby. Step stools, cushions, benches and boulders will be available for seating while outside. Outside noise ranges from subtle to loud.

records.title: Watercolor Painting: Wet Brush Techniques
records.venue_name: Environmental Education Center
records.description:
Are you new to watercolors? Have you dabbled in it and want to practice different brush techniques? Join Brooklyn Bridge Park educators and learn different ways to use your brushes and apply paint.
In Session 1 (on December 6) we will focus on wet brush techniques and in
Session 2 (on December 13)
we will focus on dry brush techniques. In both, we will be applying what we learn towards botanical art.
Please note that you
DO NOT
have to attend both sessions.
No previous experience necessary. This workshop is best suited for ages 13 and up. All materials will be provided, but if you have a favorite watercolor brush, feel free to bring it. The event is first-come, first-serve with 25 spots available. Advanced registration is encouraged but not required.
Register Now!
Accessibility Note: Please reach out to education@bbp.nyc for any accessibility needs or questions. The workshop will take place at the Environmental Education Center at 99 Plymouth Street, which is an accessible building. The classroom itself has a low-pile carpet. Seating is on stools. records.title: Watercolor Painting: Dry Brush Techniques
records.venue_name: Environmental Education Center
records.description:
Are you new to watercolors? Have you dabbled in it and want to practice different brush techniques? Join Brooklyn Bridge Park educators and learn different ways to use your brushes and apply paint.
In
Session 1 (on December 6)
we will focus on wet brush techniques and in Session 2 (on December 13) we will focus on dry brush techniques. In both, we will be applying what we learn towards botanical art.

DO NOT
have to attend both sessions.

Register Now!

records.title: Yoga 4 Climbers / Slow Flow + Arm Balances
records.venue_name: Ritual Moves - Yoga Room
records.description:
A 60-minute vinyasa style class for all levels, with a playful twist.
Expect a slow-build of to wake up wrists, hips, and shoulders. Build body awareness, tap in to full-body activation, and learn how to stack your joints for effortless arm balances.
Room is heated at 85-95 degrees.
Hosted in the Ritual Moves Mat Room (around the corner from BKUP at 32 Pearl Street).
Location: Ritual Moves - Yoga Room
Check in at the BKUP front desk at 20 John Street first, and then head around the corner to Ritual Moves.
Instructor
Nikki DeCarlo
I specialize in helping climbers level up technique, mobility, and mindset. We'll identify the things keeping you stuck at a plateau and make a plan to break through. I love working with women, short people, and beginner-intermediate climbers to help you establish a solid foundation, build momentum, and jumpstart your climbing journey.
My coaching style lives at the intersection of movement & well-being. I combine exercise science, mobility, & positive psychology to fast-track you to your future self. Together, we’ll establish a foundation and sustainable system for growth that you’ll actually stick to and enjoy.
Nikki also offers 1:1 coaching
→
Late-cancel / no-show fee

Waiver required for all climbers
First-time visitors must complete orientation

records.title: Inverted: Upper-Body & Core Conditioning
records.venue_name: Brooklyn Uprising
records.description:
Struggling with strength-based climbs? Want to build upper-body and core strength in a new and exciting way? Want to learn a handstand along the way? This class is built around handstand conditioning drills that develop mind-body connection, strengthen your upper body, and build the tension needed on the wall.
Instructor
Alena Pureskina
I coach
beginner
and
intermediate
climbers to build strength, improve movement, and develop a stronger climbing mindset.
My approach combines climbing technique with calisthenics and functional movement to help you understand your body, move more efficiently, and build strength that translates directly to the wall. We’ll work on technique, body awareness, strength, confidence, and the mental barriers that can hold you back.
My goal is to help you climb stronger, move smarter, and trust yourself on the wall
Alena also offers 1:1 coaching

records.title: What Grade Is It Anyway? Setter Office Hours and Community Night
records.venue_name: Brooklyn Uprising
records.description:
Ever climbed something and wondered who decided it was a V4? This community night pulls back the curtain on grading.
We'll kick things off with a discussion with our setters on how they think through grading — what they're weighing, what makes a grade go up or down, and why it's never an exact science.
Then we'll climb through a set of boulders on each wall, and we'll have an easygoing conversation on how the grade reflects (or doesn't!) your experience. Join Carly for a fun, social night that demystifies the grading process and shows just how subjective grades really are.
Discussion starts at 5:45 with community grading exercise beginning at 6:30. See you there!

records.venue_name: Brooklyn Uprising
records.description:

FAQ
What is NYRR Open Run?
NYRR Open Run is a community-based, volunteer-supported running initiative - bringing free weekly runs and walks to local neighborhood parks.
What day and time is Open Run?
Most Open Runs take place during the weekend and they start at different times in different locations. Check the schedule to see when Open Run starts in your local park.
How much does Open Run cost?
NYRR Open Run is completely free.
Do I need to be a runner?
No, you don’t need to be a runner to participate in Open Run! You can run or walk, whatever distance you feel comfortable with. We welcome people of all abilities. The key is just to get moving and have a good time.
Can I bring my dog?
Absolutely! We welcome all dogs at Open Run, as long as they are on a short leash to comply with NYC Parks regulations as well as for the safety of the other participants.
Can I bring a stroller?
Please do! We welcome all ages at Open Run. Please start toward the back and be mindful of other Open Run participants and park users.
Can I bring family and friends?
We won’t say it is a requirement, but isn’t it just more fun to run with others? Bring as many family members and friends as you wish—all are welcome at Open Run! Please keep in mind that we will be adhering to social distancing guidelines at all Open Runs.
Can I bring my kids?
Yes, you can. We ask that you run with your kids if they cannot complete the distance on their own. Please note: A parent or guardian must also sign a waiver before any child under age 18 can participate.
How can I volunteer at Open Run?
Visit each Open Run park's information page to sign up for a volunteer opportunity, or you can sign up through our
volunteer form
. All volunteers must sign up in advance to volunteer at an Open Run session. All volunteers should adhere to
NYRR's Volunteer Guidelines
.
Does volunteering at Open Run count toward my 9+1?
Open Run volunteer opportunities are not eligible for +1 credit for guaranteed entry ti the TCS New York City Marathon.

records.venue_name: Inwood Hill Park Open Run (approximate meeting point)
records.venue_address: Isham Street & Seaman Avenue, New York, NY 10034
records.description:
Park entrance at the intersection of Isham Street and Seaman Avenue.
Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.
Saturdays at 09:00 AM, Manhattan - Park entrance at the intersection of Isham Street and Seaman Avenue

records.description:
Park Entrance at E 149th Street (Between St. Ann’s Ave and Eagle Ave).
St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

records.venue_name: Inwood Hill Park Open Run (approximate meeting point)
records.venue_address: Isham Street & Seaman Avenue, New York, NY 10034
records.description:
Park entrance at the intersection of Isham Street and Seaman Avenue.
Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.

St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.
Saturdays at 09:00 AM, The Bronx - Park Entrance at E 149th Street (Between St. Ann’s Ave and Eagle Ave)

(opens in a new tab)
Check-in 15 mins prior to start time.

FAQ
What is NYRR Open Run?
NYRR Open Run is a community-based, volunteer-supported running initiative - bringing free weekly runs and walks to local neighborhood parks.
What day and time is Open Run?
Most Open Runs take place during the weekend and they start at different times in different locations. Check the schedule to see when Open Run starts in your local park.
How much does Open Run cost?
NYRR Open Run is completely free.
Do I need to be a runner?
No, you don’t need to be a runner to participate in Open Run! You can run or walk, whatever distance you feel comfortable with. We welcome people of all abilities. The key is just to get moving and have a good time.
Can I bring my dog?
Absolutely! We welcome all dogs at Open Run, as long as they are on a short leash to comply with NYC Parks regulations as well as for the safety of the other participants.
Can I bring a stroller?
Please do! We welcome all ages at Open Run. Please start toward the back and be mindful of other Open Run participants and park users.
Can I bring family and friends?
We won’t say it is a requirement, but isn’t it just more fun to run with others? Bring as many family members and friends as you wish—all are welcome at Open Run! Please keep in mind that we will be adhering to social distancing guidelines at all Open Runs.
Can I bring my kids?
Yes, you can. We ask that you run with your kids if they cannot complete the distance on their own. Please note: A parent or guardian must also sign a waiver before any child under age 18 can participate.
How can I volunteer at Open Run?
Visit each Open Run park's information page to sign up for a volunteer opportunity, or you can sign up through our
volunteer form
. All volunteers must sign up in advance to volunteer at an Open Run session. All volunteers should adhere to
NYRR's Volunteer Guidelines
.
Does volunteering at Open Run count toward my 9+1?
Open Run volunteer opportunities are not eligible for +1 credit for guaranteed entry ti the TCS New York City Marathon.

records.venue_name: Inwood Hill Park Open Run (approximate meeting point)
records.venue_address: Isham Street & Seaman Avenue, New York, NY 10034
records.description:
Park entrance at the intersection of Isham Street and Seaman Avenue.
Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.

records.venue_address: East 149th Street & St. Anns Avenue, Bronx, NY 10455
records.description:
Park Entrance at E 149th Street (Between St. Ann’s Ave and Eagle Ave).
St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

records.venue_address: Isham Street & Seaman Avenue, New York, NY 10034
records.description:
Park entrance at the intersection of Isham Street and Seaman Avenue.
Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.

records.title: St. Mary's Park Open Run
records.venue_name: St. Mary's Park Open Run (approximate meeting point)
records.venue_address: East 149th Street & St. Anns Avenue, Bronx, NY 10455
records.description:
Park Entrance at E 149th Street (Between St. Ann’s Ave and Eagle Ave).
St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

records.description:
Park Entrance at E 149th Street (Between St. Ann’s Ave and Eagle Ave).
St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

records.venue_name: Inwood Hill Park Open Run (approximate meeting point)
records.venue_address: Isham Street & Seaman Avenue, New York, NY 10034
records.description:
Park entrance at the intersection of Isham Street and Seaman Avenue.
Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.
Saturdays at 09:00 AM, Manhattan - Park entrance at the intersection of Isham Street and Seaman Avenue

records.venue_address: Isham Street & Seaman Avenue, New York, NY 10034
records.description:
Park entrance at the intersection of Isham Street and Seaman Avenue.
Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.

Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. records.title: Nitehawk Film Series: The Devils and Castle in the Sky
records.venue_name: Nitehawk Cinema Prospect Park
records.description:
The Devils — Recent Restorations, 11:00 AM
Starring: Vanessa Redgrave, Oliver Reed, Dudley Sutton, Max Adrian, Gemma Jones, Murray Melvin 4K restoration Ken Russell’s controversial adaptation of Aldous Huxley’s The Devils of Loudun is at long last available in its full, provocative splendor. This new restoration thrillingly incorporates material that was originally censored—footage that Russell deemed some of the best and most political work of his career. A young Derek Jarman designed the sets that house this story of a vengeful nun (Vanessa Redgrave) who accuses a priest (Oliver Reed) of collaborating with the devil, resulting in the apparent possession of an entire convent. A fearless account of state and church corruption, The Devils mixes graphic sexual imagery with religious iconography in an unforgettable spectacle that could only issue from the mind of Ken Russell. Following its NYFF64 premiere, The Devils will open on 35mm for a one-week engagement beginning October 16 at Film at Lincoln Center. A Warner Bros. Clockwork release. (Directed by Ken Russell, 1971, 114 min., DCP, Rated NC-17.) Film series: Recent Restorations / The Anniversary Party / Brunch Movies.
Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com
Castle in the Sky — 35mm Screenings, 12:00 PM
Starring: Anna Paquin, James Van Der Beek, Cloris Leachman, Mark Hamill, Mandy Patinkin Castle in the Sky is a timeless story of courage and friendship, with stunning animation from acclaimed Academy Award-winning director Hayao Miyazaki. This high-flying adventure begins when Pazu, an engineer’s apprentice, spies a young girl, Sheeta, floating down from the sky, held aloft by a glowing pendant. Both Sheeta and Pazu are searching for the legendary floating castle, Laputa, and they vow to travel there together to unravel the mystery of the luminous crystal. But their quest won’t be easy, as soon they are being pursued by greedy air pirates, the military, and secret government agents, who all seek the power Sheeta alone can control. (Directed by Hayao Miyazaki, 1986, 124 min., 35mm, Rated PG.) Film series: 35mm Screenings / Family Friendly / Nostalgia, Ultra. / The Anniversary Party / Brunch Movies.
Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com

records.title: Nitehawk: NoBudge Live 53 — Shorts
records.venue_name: Nitehawk Cinema Prospect Park
records.description:
NoBudge Live 53 — Shorts, 7:00 PM
NoBudge is happy to present a program of eight short films from a group of emerging indie filmmakers mostly based in New York. The lineup focuses on narrative dramas and comedies exploring a range of styles and tones. Six of the films are NYC or Brooklyn premieres and all filmmakers will be in attendance for a post-screening Q&A and Afterparty. NoBudge is an online platform spotlighting the best in low-budget indie filmmaking. “One of the best places to sample what’s happening in low-budget cinema worldwide,” says Glenn Kenny of The New York Times. Its mission is to provide a supportive home for emerging indie filmmakers working with limited resources and without major industry connections, and to be a trusted discovery platform. All My Idols are Fat NYC Premiere . Director Neha Simon in person. Two friends stumble into finding out how close their relationship really is. (12 min) Plastic Glass Brooklyn Premiere. Director Mitchell Clark in person. Careening through a day in the life of a high schooler, a teenager and his friends experiment with a mysterious drug-like substance. (15 min) Behind this Locked Door Director Matthew Brennan in person. When a woman moves in with her boyfriend, she discovers he spends a concerning amount of time in the bathroom. (13 min) Period Piece Brooklyn Premiere. Director Flora Nolan in person. When her period abruptly stops, a young woman reckons with her body and reflects on her expectations of womanhood. (12 min) Making Love Songs Brooklyn Premiere . Directors Leon and Daniel Brodsky in person. A teenager is commissioned to photograph a series of disturbing events. (17 min) Faux Amis NYC Premiere. Director Theodore Matza in person. Two twenty-somethings travel to Paris so that one of them can connect with an Instagram boyfriend. (15 min) Fix Director Vogue Giambri in person. Do you run around late at night looking for your fix? (15 min) Whoa NYC Premiere. Director Elizabeth O’Donnell in person. A baby-boomer mom and her millennial daughter take psilocybin mushrooms together. (13 min) (2026, 112 min., DCP.) Film series: Shorts.
Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com

records.title: Nitehawk: The Thing — 35mm Screenings
records.venue_name: Nitehawk Cinema Prospect Park
records.description:
The Thing — 35mm Screenings, 9:15 PM
Starring: Kurt Russell, Wilford Brimley, Keith David, David Clennon, T.K. Carter Snuggle up! Kurt Russell battles against the cold and a mysterious alien life-form in the John Carpenter version of The Thing . A team of scientists working in the frozen landscape of the Antarctic encounter a shape-shifting and killer alien being after a strange dog enters the camp. This is, of course, after witnessing a Norwegian team chasing the dog to kill it but perish in a helicopter crash before they can and before they can explain. Isolated in a part of the world nearly as remote as space, Kurt Russell’s R.J. MacReady leads the charge for survival not just his team but for the entire human race. Overshadowed upon its release by the more family friendly film E.T., Carpenter’s The Thing is a terrifying look at outer space in our own world that combines brilliant special effects and humorously scary scenes to punctuate this contemporary version of The Thing from Another World . (Directed by John Carpenter, 1982, 109 min., 35mm, Rated R.) Film series: 35mm Screenings / Re-Consider This!.
Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com

records.title: Nitehawk Film Series: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring and Tally Brown, New York
records.venue_name: Nitehawk Cinema Prospect Park
records.description:
The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring — 35mm Screenings, 11:00 AM
Starring: Elijah Wood, Ian McKellen, Liv Tyler, Viggo Mortensen, Sean Astin, Cate Blanchett The future of civilization rests in the fate of the One Ring, which has been lost for centuries. Powerful forces are unrelenting in their search for it. But fate has placed it in the hands of a young Hobbit named Frodo Baggins (Elijah Wood), who inherits the Ring and steps into legend. A daunting task lies ahead for Frodo when he becomes the Ringbearer – to destroy the One Ring in the fires of Mount Doom where it was forged. (Directed by Peter Jackson, 2001, 178 min., 35mm, Rated PG 13.) Film series: 35mm Screenings / The Anniversary Party / Brunch Movies.
Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com
Tally Brown, New York — Recent Restorations, 12:15 PM
2K restoration by the Deutsche Kinemathek “The bewigged Miss Brown, with false eyelashes capable of sending her short, round body aloft, is the most memorable raconteur and cabaret artist you’ll hear all year.” – Melissa Anderson, The Village Voice Both a loving portrait of a larger-than-life personality and a vivid record of New York’s 1970s downtown demimonde, this captivating documentary follows Tally Brown—cabaret chanteuse, underground film star, and a staple of Andy Warhol’s Factory—as she takes filmmaker Rosa von Praunheim on a tour through the grit and glamour of the city that made her. Capturing Brown’s mesmerizing performances (including her breathtaking bilingual cover of David Bowie’s “Heroes”) as well as her social world among fellow queer cult icons like Holly Woodlawn, Divine, and Taylor Mead, Tally Brown, New York is an essential snapshot of a scene that has passed into legend. (Directed by Rosa von Praunheim, 1979, 101 min., DCP, Rated NR.) Film series: Recent Restorations / Representation.
Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com

Capturing Brown’s mesmerizing performances (including her breathtaking bilingual cover of David Bowie’s “Heroes”) as well as her social world among fellow queer cult icons like Holly Woodlawn, Divine, and Taylor Mead, Tally Brown, New York is an essential snapshot of a scene that has passed into legend. (Directed by Rosa von Praunheim, 1979, 101 min., DCP, Rated NR.) Film series: Recent Restorations / Representation.

Oliver meets the irreverent and unpredictable Anna (Mélanie Laurent) only months after his father Hal Fields (Christopher Plummer) has passed away. Starring: Miyoko Shôji, Shôzô Îzuka, Mami Koyama Experience the gorgeous new restoration of what many believe to be Satoshi Kon’s ( Perfect Blue, Paprika, Tokyo Godfathers ) greatest work, Millennium Actress . When the legendary Ginei Studios shuts down, filmmaker Genya Tachibana and his assistant are tasked with interviewing its reclusive star, Chiyoko Fujiwara, who had retired from the spotlight 30 years prior. As she recounts her career, Genya and his crew are literally pulled into her memories where they witness her chance encounter with a mysterious man on the run from the police. Despite never knowing his name or his face, Chiyoko relentlessly pursues that man in a seamless blend of reality and memory that only Satoshi Kon could deliver. Boasting countless awards, including the Grand Prize in the Japan Agency of Cultural Affairs Media Arts Festival, which it shared with Hayao Miyazaki’s Spirited Away , Millennium Actress is a must-see for anime fans of all ages. records.title: Nitehawk: Once Upon a Time in Harlem — Adventures in Black Cinema
records.venue_name: Nitehawk Cinema Prospect Park
records.description:
Once Upon a Time in Harlem — Adventures in Black Cinema, 7:00 PM
A decade after his death, genre-defying filmmaker William Greaves has one last trick up his sleeve with what he considered the most important event he captured on film: a 1972 party he engineered with the living luminaries of the Harlem Renaissance. For four hours, this extraordinary group – many of whom had not seen each other in fifty years – reminisced, critiqued, argued, laughed and drank while wrestling with their place in a rapidly shifting cultural landscape. Shot on 16mm film, newly restored and now directed by Greaves’ son David, this landmark film is at once a self-exploration and an inquiry into the heart of the critical mass of energy called the Harlem Renaissance. William Greaves’ intent was not only to document these artists and intellectuals as they spoke about their lives and work but also to plumb the meaning of the extraordinary creative period in which they lived to help us better understand how culture has been passed on from one generation to another and the role that the artist plays in keeping it alive. (Directed by David Greaves, 2026, 100 min., DCP, Rated PG 13.) Film series: Adventures in Black Cinema / ICYMI.
Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com

Warning: Images are not from the movies we’re showing. Trust us, you can’t imagine what we’re showing! A career-making film from the late-90s, this caper flick rarely gets screened, but it turned out to be a landmark for both its director and its stars. An anthem to urban loneliness, job dissatisfaction, and unconsummated romance, it’s as light on its feet as Ocean’s 11 , as stylish as North By Northwest , and as heart-achingly emotional as a Cantopop power ballad. Featuring two of Hong Kong’s biggest stars playing lonely men who re-discover their love of life by shooting at each other, it’s a rousing, ridiculous, over-the-top supernova of fun, that reminds us this holiday season that what we have to be thankful for are Hong Kong movies. (93 min., 35mm.) Film series: Sundays on Fire.

records.title: World Day of Remembrance for Traffic Violence Victims 2026
records.venue_name: Charles A. Dana Discovery Center (approximate meeting point)
records.venue_address: Central Park North & Fifth Avenue, New York, NY 10029
records.description:
Join Families for Safe Streets as we commemorate World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims in Central Park at the Charles A. Dana Discovery Center.
This year our ceremony will include an ancient tradition from Japan, folded paper cranes. The practice of folding a thousand paper cranes was originally an endeavor undertaken to with for a long life for oneself of a loved one.
Over time, the tradition has evolved to be associated with wishing for recovery from illness or injury, for happiness and good luck or for world peace. Members of Families for Safe Streets will create a thousand origami cranes to honor loved ones killed or injured by traffic violence and the people killed or injured this past year. We look forward to seeing you to mark this solemn, meaningful day with us.
After the ceremony, Families for Safe Streets members will gather for a meal together.

records.title: TA Youth Monthly Meeting
records.venue_name: Transportation Alternatives
records.venue_address: 111 John Street Suite 260, New York, NY 10038
records.description:
**Join the Transportation Alternatives Youth Committee (TAYAC)!**
**Together, we can transform our streets into safe, sustainable, and equitable places to walk, bike, take transit, gather, and thrive.**
TAYAC is a volunteer-led committee made up of NYC teens working to make streets safer, more accessible, and people-centered, especially for the youth of our city. We meet on the **Last Friday of every month** (adjusted for holidays) to plan local campaigns, organize events, and push for better transportation options.
Our meetings are held **in person**, with a **hybrid option available** for those who prefer to join virtually. The in-person location is typically the Transportation Alternative's Office (near the Fulton Subway Stop in lower Manhattan).
Whether you’re passionate about bike lanes, safer crosswalks, or accessible sidewalks, your voice matters. Connect with a community dedicated to building a safer, more sustainable NYC. No experience is necessary—just your energy and commitment!
**Register now to join our next meeting—we can’t wait to meet you!**

records.title: Exit 12N Walk
records.venue_name: West 116th Street & Riverside Drive (approximate meeting point)
records.venue_address: West 116th Street & Riverside Drive, New York, NY 10027
records.description:
Join Transportation Alternatives, Spherical Harmonics, and Open Plans for a walk to explore Exit 12N of the Henry Hudson Parkway. Exit 12N is nestled in between the Henry Hudson Expressway and Riverside Park on parkland. It has been closed for over since July 2025 with no harm to or complaints from the community.
We want to explore turning this space back to the community as a space to walk, gather, increase climate resiliency or more! We are only limited by our imagination and our enthusiasm. As we explore the space, let us know how you would like it to be used.
We will meet at 116th Street and Riverside drive. We will walk towards the Riverside Park Tennis Courts where we can see exit 12N.
There is some rough terrain and steep inclines on the walk. Please dress according to the weather. There is a ramp down to the tennis courts and a narrow path to see the exit roadway, and bike racks next to the tennis courts. Bikes are welcome but we encourage you to lock them at the tennis court and continue the walk with us on foot.

records.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
records.venue_name: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
records.category: History, Tours, It's My Park, Seniors
records.description:
Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.
Contact phone: 7189846046

records.title: Old Stone House: Open Hours

records.description:
Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! records.title: Volunteer Workday: Fantasy Garden
records.venue_name: Fantasy Garden
records.description:
Join Fantasy Garden and NYC Parks GreenThumb for a volunteer day cleaning up the garden, rebuilding raised beds (no power tools needed), and planting native flowers! We'll provide all the tools, training, and guidance to ensure a productive and safe volunteer day. Please wear sturdy work shoes and weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks. Note some tasks will involve lifting heavy materials and extended periods of bending, squatting, and moving.Register here!Fantasy Garden has been a public green space in the Brownsville for nearly three decades, providing the community with access to free programming, volunteer opportunities, and a connection to nature. If you've been curious about urban gardening, this is a great opportunity for hands-on learning while helping your community!For information about group volunteering, please contact GreenThumb's Volunteer Program Team at gt.volunteer@parks.nyc.gov or (332) 280-4408.This event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. GreenThumb community gardens are organized, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.
Registration link: https://www.nycgovparks.org/reg/greenthumb-volunteer-events/20937
Contact phone: (332) 280-4408

records.title: My Vietnam: An Author Talk with Joan Furey RN, MA
records.venue_name: Bayside Historical Society (in Fort Totten Park)
records.description:
The Bayside Historical Society honors our veterans this November by welcoming Joan Furey, RN, MA, to The Castle for a special author presentation. Furey served in Vietnam with the U.S. Army Nurse Corps from January 1969 to January 1970.In her presentation, Furey will share what led her to join the U.S. Army in 1968 and volunteer for duty in Vietnam. Through personal anecdotes, historical context about women who served in Vietnam, and a brief slideshow, she will explore the experiences of military nurses during the Vietnam War. She will also discuss the origins of the book she co-edited with Lynda VanDevanter, Visions of War: Dreams of Peace, The Writings of Women in the Vietnam War, and read selected pieces from the collection. A Q&A and book signing will follow.Cost is $5 for BHS members and $10 for non-members; veterans are admitted free.Purchase tickets online at www.baysidehistorical.org/events-1/my-vietnam-an-author-talk-with-joan-furey-rn-maThis event is part of the Bayside Historical Society's Author Talk at the Castle Series.

records.title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
records.venue_name: Old Stone House (in Washington Park)
records.description:
Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.
Contact phone: 718-768-3195

records.title: Proximity Exhibition
records.venue_name: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center) (approximate meeting point)
records.description: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another.  When: October 2 - December 13Fridays & Saturdays, 12:00 PM-7:00 PM | Sundays, 11:00 AM- 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building C  (View Site Map and Directions)Admission:$5.00 – General Admission$4.00 – Students/SeniorsPlease note: On October 16, we will host an opening reception for PROXIMITY from 6-8 PM. Visiting during those hours will be free. Please RSVP to the reception here: https://snug-harbor.org/event/proximity-opening-reception/ PROXIMITY is made possible through generous support from the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature, the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council, and the Samuel I. Newhouse Foundation.

records.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
records.venue_name: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
records.category: History, Tours, It's My Park, Seniors
records.description:
Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.
Contact phone: 7189846046

records.title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
records.venue_name: Old Stone House (in Washington Park)
records.description:
Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

records.description: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another.  When: October 2 - December 13Fridays & Saturdays, 12:00 PM-7:00 PM | Sundays, 11:00 AM- 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building C  (View Site Map and Directions)Admission:$5.00 – General Admission$4.00 – Students/SeniorsPlease note: On October 16, we will host an opening reception for PROXIMITY from 6-8 PM. Visiting during those hours will be free. Please RSVP to the reception here: https://snug-harbor.org/event/proximity-opening-reception/ PROXIMITY is made possible through generous support from the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature, the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council, and the Samuel I. Newhouse Foundation.

records.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
records.venue_name: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
records.category: History, Tours, It's My Park, Seniors
records.description:
Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.
Contact phone: 7189846046

records.title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
records.venue_name: Old Stone House (in Washington Park)
records.description:
Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.
Contact phone: 718-768-3195

records.title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
records.venue_name: Old Stone House (in Washington Park)
records.description:
Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.
Contact phone: 718-768-3195

records.title: Proximity Exhibition
records.venue_name: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center) (approximate meeting point)
records.description: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another.  When: October 2 - December 13Fridays & Saturdays, 12:00 PM-7:00 PM | Sundays, 11:00 AM- 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building C  (View Site Map and Directions)Admission:$5.00 – General Admission$4.00 – Students/SeniorsPlease note: On October 16, we will host an opening reception for PROXIMITY from 6-8 PM. Visiting during those hours will be free. Please RSVP to the reception here: https://snug-harbor.org/event/proximity-opening-reception/ PROXIMITY is made possible through generous support from the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature, the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council, and the Samuel I. Newhouse Foundation.

records.title: A Christmas Carol at the Merchant's House
records.venue_name: Merchant's House Museum
records.description:
In December 1867, Charles Dickens arrived in New York City for a month of sold-out performances of his beloved holiday classic, A Christmas Carol. As the New York Herald exclaimed, “The Christmas Carol becomes doubly enchanting when one hears it performed by Dickens.”Join Mr. Dickens, portrayed by John Kevin Jones and Vince Gatton (at alternating performances), as he tells his timeless Christmas tale in the elegant intact Greek Revival double parlor of the landmark 1832 Merchant’s House Museum.Surrounded by 19th century holiday decorations, flickering candles, and richly appointed period furnishings, audiences will be transported back 150 years in this captivating performance created from Dickens’ own script. Doors open 30 minutes prior to performance.A Christmas Reception with Mr. Dickens! Toast the season with a cup of “Smoking Bishop” (mulled wine) and enjoy a special performance of “A Visit from St. Nicholas” by Mr. Dickens himself. The 19th century family room, kitchen, and garden (weather permitting) will be open to guests during the reception. Tickets $35. Select performances only. Limited capacity. Doors open 60 minutes prior to performance for Reception.Tickets $50 – $130. Run-time 70 minutes.
Registration link: https://ci.ovationtix.com/35240/production/1288280
